body:
# Add Continuous Testing with GitHub Actions

This PR introduces comprehensive continuous integration and testing workflows using GitHub Actions to ensure code quality and cross-platform compatibility.

## Changes

### 🚀 New GitHub Actions Workflows

1. **CI Workflow** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
   - Tests on Node.js versions 16.x, 18.x, and 20.x
   - Runs on every push to main/master branches and PRs
   - Includes dependency installation, testing, and build verification
   - Separate lint and format job for code quality checks

2. **Cross-Platform Testing** (`.github/workflows/cross-platform.yml`)
   - Tests on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS
   - Ensures the library works correctly across different operating systems
   - Important for an Xcode-related library that may be used in various development environments

## Benefits

- ✅ **Automated Testing**: Every PR and push automatically runs the full test suite
- ✅ **Multi-Node Support**: Ensures compatibility with Node.js 16, 18, and 20
- ✅ **Cross-Platform**: Verifies functionality on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS
- ✅ **Build Verification**: Confirms TypeScript compilation succeeds
- ✅ **Fast Feedback**: Developers get immediate feedback on code changes

## Testing

The workflows use the existing Jest test suite with 105 tests covering:
- pbxproj parsing and manipulation
- Model-based API functionality
- Swift Package Manager support
- FileSystemSynchronized objects
- Build configuration handling

All tests are currently passing ✅

## Dependencies

Uses Yarn with frozen lockfile for consistent, reproducible builds across all environments.

# Pull Request Template

## 📄 Description

Update ICR CarbonProject and Credit generation to allow dynamic generation of usable ICR project ids and CarbonProjects.

`ProjectCreated`
ProjectCreated event now creates the data source only. 

CarbonProjects are stored in the subgraph with registry-id-vintage id, which we derive from the serialization which is unavailable in `ProjectCreated`. Therefore we cannot create the actual CarbonProject entity from this event.

This PR deactivates the `compute_initial_i_dkg_dealings` endpoint from the management canister, since it has been superseded by the `reshare_chain_key` endpoint, and the registry canister has been migrated to use the new endpoint. 

In particular this PR:
- Makes all calls to `compute_initial_i_dkg_dealings` fail
- Migrates some leftover test-cases to use `reshare_chain_key` calls instead
- Removes the routing logic of the call, and instead directs the call to the own subnet

In a followup PR, I will remove the logic from consensus to process the call. Since this is an internal API and we know that it has not been in use since the registry canister was migrated, we know that there are no open contexts and the whole removal could happen in one PR, however, I still think it makes sense to split this into 2 PRs, to be easier to review.

# PR overview

For LWP100-1464.

Currently has a bunch of additional code for outputting the coordinate that a setCoordinate node is connected to, this will be removed from this PR and a new ticket created.

## Testing

Currently mostly making use of existed jammed tests, additional tests are partially complete.

# Commit message

Allow tail loops to be fused.

Previously fusing tail loops could not be done, so tail loops were not added for jammed tests as the unrolling of the X and Y loops caused multiple tail loops to exist. This PR fixes this issue, and also adds a new graph constraint that any given node cannot be in the body of two nodes which are not themselves nested in some order (i.e. if A is in the body of both B and C, either B is in the body of C or vice versa).

author: copilot
body:
This PR resolves the dependency resolution issue when installing `@blossom-carousel/react` in projects using React v19.x or Next.js v15+.

## Problem

Users encountered `ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree` errors when trying to install the package with React v19:

```sh
npm error ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer react@"^18.0.0" from @blossom-carousel/react@0.1.10
npm error Found: react@19.1.0
```

This forced users to use `--force` or `--legacy-peer-deps` flags, which is not ideal for production environments.

## Solution

Updated the peer dependencies in `packages/react/package.json` to support both React 18 and React 19:

```diff
"peerDependencies": {
-  "react": "^18.0.0",
-  "react-dom": "^18.0.0"
+  "react": "^18.0.0 || >=19.0.0-0",
+  "react-dom": "^18.0.0 || >=19.0.0-0"
}
```

The version range `>=19.0.0-0` ensures compatibility with:
- React v19 stable releases (`19.1.0`, `19.2.0`, etc.)
- React v19 pre-release versions (`19.0.0-rc-*`) used by Next.js v15

## Testing

✅ Package builds successfully with no changes to component code  
✅ Compatible with React 18.3.1  
✅ Compatible with React 19.1.0  
✅ Compatible with React 19 RC versions (Next.js 15)  
✅ No breaking changes - existing React 18 projects continue to work

The BlossomCarousel component uses only stable React APIs (`useEffect`, `useRef`, JSX) that are fully backward compatible across these versions.

Fixes #5.

author: yanisamarouayache
body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the hotel scraping and storage functionality, including backend updates for price history tracking and frontend improvements for user interaction and feedback. Key changes include the addition of a `PriceStorageService` for managing scraped data, new endpoints for scraping and storing hotel data, and frontend components for displaying scrape results.

### Backend Changes

#### New Services and Endpoints:
* Added `PriceStorageService` to handle hotel and price storage, ensuring price history is preserved. It uses `PrismaService` to upsert hotel data and insert daily prices only when changes are detected (`apps/backend/src/scraper/price-storage.service.ts`).
* Updated `ScraperController` with two new endpoints: 
  * [`/hotel/scrape-and-store`](diffhunk://#diff-3472654c238765baf7517f922cd15a4896d51cc55e5487b2803953e38585f2b9R43-R88): Scrapes a single hotel and stores its data.
  * [`/batch/scrape-and-store`](diffhunk://#diff-3472654c238765baf7517f922cd15a4896d51cc55e5487b2803953e38585f2b9R110-R156): Scrapes and stores data for multiple hotels.

#### Module and Service Updates:
* Updated `ScraperModule` to include `PriceStorageService` in providers and exports (`apps/backend/src/scraper/scraper.module.ts`).
* Minor refactoring in `ScraperService` to clarify its role in scraping without database logic (`apps/backend/src/scraper/scraper.service.ts`).

### Frontend Changes

#### New Components and Features:
* Introduced `ScrapeResultDialog` to display scrape results and errors in a dialog (`apps/frontend/hotel-intel/src/components/Dialog/ScrapeResultDialog.tsx`).
* Enhanced `HotelCard` with a "Scraper & Stocker" button to trigger scraping and display progress and results. Added loading states and progress bars for better user feedback (`apps/frontend/hotel-intel/src/components/HotelCard/HotelCard.tsx`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-571d63df75f2b5f7c98f2ca94a1a8bbc2f403d2c98fd37d11450f009b9de60cfR63-R161) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-571d63df75f2b5f7c98f2ca94a1a8bbc2f403d2c98fd37d11450f009b9de60cfL129-R255)

#### GraphQL Updates:
* Extended GraphQL queries and mutations to include the `url` field for hotels, enabling scraping operations (`apps/frontend/hotel-intel/src/graphql/queries.ts`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f999ad0eb4f3fed017022bbd3323980ed09745a3199f03edf5da334fdb4e4dc0R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f999ad0eb4f3fed017022bbd3323980ed09745a3199f03edf5da334fdb4e4dc0R52) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f999ad0eb4f3fed017022bbd3323980ed09745a3199f03edf5da334fdb4e4dc0R86)

These changes collectively improve the system's ability to scrape, store, and manage hotel data while enhancing the user experience with clear feedback mechanisms.

author: michaelthemay
body:
### Pull Request Description

**Intent:** Improve the handling of pasted text in the application by leveraging an LLM to dynamically determine the syntax style and generate a concise summary, enhancing user experience in the GUI and making context fragments more accurate.

**Behavior Changes:**
- When text is pasted, it now uses LLM analysis to infer the syntax style (e.g., from predefined constants) and create a one-line summary, replacing default styles like "text/plain".
- The system retries up to 3 times if the LLM returns an invalid syntax style, falling back to defaults on failure to ensure robustness.
- In WorkspacePanel, pasted content is added with asynchronous analysis futures, avoiding UI blocking.

**Key Implementation Ideas:**
- Utilized Langchain4j's tool-calling mechanism to define a tool for LLM interactions, with error handling for JSON parsing and invalid responses.
- Updated ContextFragment to store and resolve syntax style via CompletableFuture, keeping it dynamic without serializing in DTOs.
- Extracted valid syntax styles from SyntaxConstants for validation, promoting maintainability. (112 words)

## Summary
Fixed NFT summary calculation to use `totalBalance` instead of `balance` field to include reserved tokens in floor price estimation.

## Changes  
- Changed `token_account.balance` to `token_account.totalBalance` in accounts NFT summary query
- This ensures reserved tokens are included in floor price calculations

## Technical Details
The `totalBalance` field represents the complete token holdings (available + reserved tokens) while `balance` only includes immediately available tokens. For floor price estimation, we need to consider the total token holdings to provide accurate value calculations.

Database relationship: `totalBalance = balance + reservedBalance`

## Motivation (prefer a non-technical explanation)

O preview do cartão de crédito não estava condizendo com o valor digitado no campo: 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36356358-1df3-4a4f-a417-200fc147da44)

Além disso, ao colar um valor de cartão sobre outro cartão, acabava truncando parte do valor para caber no tamanho anterior. Foi resolvido.

Coloquei na pipe para notificar as traduções no checkout no canal do slack, infra criou as envs.

Tivemos um caso de um cliente com uma imagem maior do que o max-width que limitávamos no css dela. A partir de agora, não podemos usar o max-with pq ele faz qualquer imagem com tamanho superior se redimensionar, causando uma piscada na tela. Para isso resolvi tbm com fit-contain e definindo um loading para a imagem quando ainda não tiver carregada, não exibir (a príncipio estou aberta a sugestões)

## Proposed solution (including technical details and their motivations)

Criei uma nova função chamada applyMask que lida certinho com o valor digitado dentro do preview do cartão usando a lib cardValidator. 
Criei o evento de onPaste que não tava criado no checkout-text-field, o que fazia os onPastes dos componentes pais não funcionarem corretamente.

## Observations (optional - any additional information you deem important)

Time de design já validou o preview do cartão:

This pull request introduces significant refactoring across multiple controller classes and DTOs in the project. The changes focus on improving code structure, enhancing DTO usage for better data encapsulation, and simplifying request and response handling. Key updates include replacing traditional DTO classes with Java `record` types, restructuring controller methods to use more specific DTOs, and removing unused imports and methods.

### Controller Updates:

#### Article Controller:
* Refactored `getAllArticles` and `createArticle` methods to use `ArticleDto.Basic` and `ArticleDto.Detailed` respectively, ensuring more concise and targeted responses.
* Replaced `SecurityContextHolder` authentication with `@AuthenticationPrincipal` for cleaner user access in `createArticle`.

#### Authentication Controller:
* Updated `registerUser`, `loginUser`, and `authenticatedUser` methods to use detailed DTOs (`UserDto.Detailed`) for responses, improving clarity and consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c83c8db0317d41a5c4ff040150a16ff7110cad2fcb0593743cb328247e064443L46-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c83c8db0317d41a5c4ff040150a16ff7110cad2fcb0593743cb328247e064443L66-R68)
* Removed redundant request DTOs (`RegisterUserRequest`, `LoginUserRequest`) in favor of nested DTOs in `UserDto`.

#### Category Controller:
* Enhanced `getAllCategories`, `getCategoryById`, and `createCategory` methods to use `CategoryDto.Detailed` for detailed responses. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5650714b3711df050dcd8ebdb88d84bf0c3a1e9e34e89a03318838d951a38b45L40-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5650714b3711df050dcd8ebdb88d84bf0c3a1e9e34e89a03318838d951a38b45L60-L82)
* Removed unused endpoints and request DTOs (`CreateCategoryRequest`, `UpdateCategoryRequest`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5650714b3711df050dcd8ebdb88d84bf0c3a1e9e34e89a03318838d951a38b45L7-L8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5650714b3711df050dcd8ebdb88d84bf0c3a1e9e34e89a03318838d951a38b45L27-L28)

#### User Controller:
* Updated `getAllUsers` and `uploadAvatar` methods to use `UserDto.Detailed` for better encapsulation of user data. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-783ee1284eafb531b1d4f169756ffd65d88ef4665945175c94c070dc09a7781aL37-R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-783ee1284eafb531b1d4f169756ffd65d88ef4665945175c94c070dc09a7781aL57-R65)

#### User Admin Controller:
* Removed the `getAllUsers` method, which was redundant with the `UserController`.

### DTO Enhancements:

#### Article DTO:
* Replaced the traditional `ArticleDto` class with multiple `record` types (`Basic`, `Detailed`, `Summary`, etc.) for specific use cases, improving clarity and reducing boilerplate code.
* Added validation annotations to request records (`CreateRequest`, `UpdateRequest`) for improved input validation.

#### Category DTO:
* Refactored `CategoryDto` into `record` types (`Basic`, `Detailed`, `CreateRequest`, etc.) to streamline data handling and validation.
* Introduced `CreateWithImageRequest` to handle multipart form data for category creation with images.

## Feature Summary

**Peer-to-Peer Review Marketplace** - A competitive bidding system where reviewers can bid on reviewing specific papers, creating a market-driven approach to academic peer review.

**Key Features:**
- Authors create marketplaces for their papers with minimum bid requirements
- Reviewers bid with proposed timelines and messages
- Automatic escrow system protects both parties
- Multiple review slots per paper
- Automatic fee collection for platform sustainability
- Overdue payment protection for reviewers

**Code Changes:** 
- 5 new data maps for marketplace operations
- 10 new public functions for marketplace interaction
- 4 new read-only functions for data retrieval
- Comprehensive error handling and validation
- Built-in escrow and payment release mechanisms

**Step-by-Step Implementation:**
1. Authors call `create-review-marketplace` to start a bidding process
2. Reviewers use `place-review-bid` to compete for review slots
3. Authors select preferred reviewers with `select-reviewer`
4. Reviewers complete work via `complete-marketplace-review`
5. Payments are released through `release-marketplace-payment`

author: cal-l
body: ## **Description** This is a PR from @Nodonisko at Margelo to make Sentry faster. Original PR - https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/pull/16025 This PR could speed up Sentry events processing around up to ~15x. I am not able to consistently reproduce slow Sentry (it depends on how much breadcrumbs and extra data are collected), but performance gain helps even when sending relatively small amounts of extra data. For small event time needed dropped from 100ms to under <10ms. For big events I randomly encountered it dropped from 1s to <100ms. In future this patch for Sentry might not be necessary, because Sentry team is working on fix in library itself, but it might take some time. There is also second part of PR modifying `metro.config.js` to use faster native polyfills, this could speed up app in some other places. ## **Related issues** Fixes: [#15560](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/issues/15560) ## **Manual testing steps** I would recommend to run smoke test across whole app because this polyfilled libraries could be used in many places eveywhere in the app. I would also recommend to verify that events from Sentry are received in Sentry dashboard. ## **Screenshots/Recordings** ### **Before** Sending big Sentry event before changes on emulator takes around 380ms. body:
Add the `--poison-value` flag to the DR client. If a value is specified though this flag, such value will be forwarded to the destination register of faulty loads during speculation, instead of just rolling back the speculation.

This is useful in cases where the faulty load's address is attacker-controlled to evaluate the presence of leak gadgets (e.g. double loads or dispatch gadgets.

### **User description** ### 🔗 Related Issues partially fixes #14291 ### 💥 What does this PR do? same as #16024 ### 🔧 Implementation Notes This pull request introduces nullability annotations to improve type safety and clarify the handling of nullable values in several exception classes within the Selenium Java codebase. The changes ensure that parameters and fields that can accept or return `null` are explicitly marked as nullable, while the classes themselves are marked as null-safe. ### Nullability Annotations Added to Exception Classes: * **`NoSuchSessionException`**: - Added `@NullMarked` annotation to the class. - Marked the `reason` parameter in constructors as `@Nullable`. * **`ScriptTimeoutException`**: - Added `@NullMarked` annotation to the class. - Marked the `message` and `cause` parameters in constructors as `@Nullable`. * **`SessionNotCreatedException`**: - Added `@NullMarked` annotation to the class. - Marked the `msg` and `cause` parameters in constructors as `@Nullable`. * **`TimeoutException`**: - Added `@NullMarked` annotation to the class. - Marked the `message` and `cause` parameters in constructors as `@Nullable`. * **`UnhandledAlertException`**: - Added `@NullMarked` annotation to the class. - Marked the `alertText` field and the `message` and `alertText` parameters in constructors as `@Nullable`. - Updated the `getAlertText` method to return `@Nullable`. ### 💡 Additional Considerations ### 🔄 Types of changes - Cleanup (formatting, renaming) ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement ___ ### **Description** - Added JSpecify nullability annotations to exception classes - Marked classes as `@NullMarked` for null safety - Annotated constructor parameters and fields as `@Nullable` - Enhanced type safety for exception handling ___ ### **Changes diagram** ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Exception Classes"] --> B["@NullMarked Annotation"] A --> C["@Nullable Parameters"] B --> D["Type Safety"] C --> D ``` ___ ### **Changes walkthrough** 📝

author: georgewrmarshall
body:
## **Description**

This PR standardizes the rest of all component `README.mdx` files within the `@metamask/design-system-react` package to align with a consistent template.

1.  **Reason for the change**: To ensure uniformity and improve developer experience by providing clear, predictable, and high-quality documentation across all components in the design system.
2.  **Improvement/Solution**: All 26 `README.mdx` files now follow a consistent structure, including:
    *   Standardized import structure for Storybook `Controls` and `Canvas`.
    *   Consistent component descriptions.
    *   **Correct placement of the usage example code snippet at the top** (after the component description and before the main `Canvas` story).
    *   Uniform prop documentation using tables (TYPE, REQUIRED, DEFAULT).
    *   Proper integration of Storybook stories and `Component API` sections.
    *   Inclusion of references to MetaMask Design System Guides.

## **Related issues**

Part of: https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-design-system/issues/488

## **Manual testing steps**

1.  Clone the repository and navigate to `packages/design-system-react`.
2.  Run `yarn install` and `yarn build`.
3.  Run `yarn storybook` to launch Storybook.
4.  In Storybook, navigate to various components (e.g., Button, Text, AvatarAccount, BadgeCount) and select their `Docs` tab.
5.  Verify that the documentation for each component follows the standardized template:
    *   The component name and description are at the top.
    *   The code usage example is immediately after the description.
    *   The `Canvas` and `Controls` blocks are present and functional.
    *   Prop tables are consistently formatted with `TYPE`, `REQUIRED`, and `DEFAULT` columns.

## **Screenshots/Recordings**

### **Before**

- Inconsistent prop documentation format
- Missing detailed prop information
- Varying documentation styles between components
- Incomplete coverage of component APIs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba869c28-031b-430a-84ba-929eac728d0f

### **After**

- Standardized prop tables with consistent formatting
- Comprehensive prop documentation with types, requirements, and defaults
- Clear, organized structure across all Avatar component documentation
- Complete coverage of all component props and their usage

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5da87ac-19e6-4487-af5f-1d07185635be

author: ian-ross
body:
**WIP: rough so far.**

Read OAG files, convert them to SQLite database, and get data out of the database in a very simple way.

There are two commands set up:

`convert-oag-data <input-csv-file> <output-sqlite-file>` takes an input OAG CSV file and produces an SQLite3 output file. This reads pre-processed OAG CSV data provided by Prateek. For example:

```
convert-oag-data /home/prateekr/Workbench/AEIC/Processed/OAG_2024_processed_AACES_2050.csv db.sqlite
```

`oag-query <db-file> <condition>...` does very simple queries on the database. For example:

```
oag-query db.sqlite carrier==DL depapt==JFK 'seats>200'
```

The output from `oag-query` is rudimentary, since this is just a demo.

There is an `OAGDatabase` class representing the database. At the moment this just has a single query function that you can pass conditions to, but it's easy enough to write more application-specific things so the query details are encapsulated.

Entries in the OAG database are represented by an `OAGEntry` dataclass. That's not quite finished (again, demo) since there are some fields that could be handled better than they currently are.

Questions:

1. Would it be better for the data conversion tool to work from the original OAG input files? Would it make sense to fold Prateek's pre-processing into the thing that makes the database?
2. What sort of query patterns might there be for this? At the moment, the only query function does simple subsetting, returning full records, i.e., equivalent to full rows in the input CSV file. Are you likely to want anything other than that?

body:
#### What is this PR About?
Some operator namespace may need extra labels. For example, recent openshift-lvm-operator need 
pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged for the operator namespace, otherwise it will fail. The ability to add the customer labels per operator will at least serve as a temp workaround.

#### How do we test this?
Provide commands/steps to test this PR.

Add the namespaceLabels in the values.yaml for test:
operatorGroups:
```
  - name: openshift-lvm-operator
    targetOwnNamespace: true
    createNamespace: true
    namespaceLabels:
      pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: privileged
      pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged
      pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: privileged
```
then use helm template . to render and verify the extra labels is indeed rendered under the namespace

* Refactors the existing `/governance-state/list` endpoint to use `handle_rest` and return only `GovActionId` in Bech32 format, instead of `GovActionId` objects and all votes stored in state. 
* Adds `/governance-state/proposal/<Bech32_GovActionId>` endpoint to return deposit, rewards_account, gov_action_id, gov_action, and anchor for a specific proposal. 
* Adds `/governance-state/proposal/<Bech32_GovActionId>/votes` endpoint to return all votes (`DataHash` and `VotingProcedures`) keyed by voter.

author: xiaotong-shen
body:
This PR wraps up the core logic for the logout functionality. In the LogoutInputData class, I fixed the username field to be final and added a getter so the interactor can pull the username out cleanly.

On the interactor side, I wired up the constructor to store the data access object and presenter properly. Then in the execute method, I implemented the full logout flow, which gets the current username from the input data, clears it from the DAO by setting it to null, and then creates a LogoutOutputData object with that username and tells the presenter to render the success view.

IMPORTANT NOTE: I’m assuming logout always succeeds, since there’s no obvious failure case if the current user is already set. Let me know if we want to handle something like that later. I wasn't too sure about this decision.

## **Description**

This PR addresses and resolves all identified ESLint warnings across the monorepo.

**Reason for Change:**
The primary reason is to improve code quality, maintain consistency, and ensure `yarn lint` runs with 0 warnings, as per the defined task.

**Improvement/Solution:**
ESLint warnings were systematically fixed using a targeted approach:
1.  **Global Variable Shadowing (`@typescript-eslint/no-shadow`)**: Suppressed for `IconName` enums in `global.d.ts` files where names intentionally shadow global types for icon representation.
2.  **Import Naming Conventions (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`)**: Suppressed for `React` namespace imports in `global.d.ts` files, as this is necessary for TypeScript declaration files.
3.  **Test Conditionals (`jest/no-conditional-in-test`)**: Suppressed in `brandColor.test.ts` where conditional logic is essential for testing different color family structures.
4.  **Unused Variables (`@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`)**: Renamed unused `args` parameters to `_args` in `Typography.stories.tsx` and added explicit typing, following best practices for intentionally unused variables.
5.  **Import Warnings (`import-x/no-named-as-default-member`)**: Updated `eslint-disable` comment in `scripts/create-package/utils.ts` to explicitly allow dynamic `require()` for `.js` config files where ESM imports are not supported.

The strategy focused on using justified inline `eslint-disable` comments for intentional patterns and making minimal, targeted code changes where actual issues (like unused variables) were present.

## **Related issues**

Fixes: https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-design-system/issues/659

1.  Run `yarn install` to ensure all dependencies are up to date.
2.  Run `yarn lint` and confirm that there are no warnings reported.
3.  Run `yarn test` and confirm that all tests pass.

## Task

Prevent all touch control schemes to appear in the ChooseInputSchemePanel when spawning a robot if the device does not support touch capabilities.

The only way to remove these is to clear all preferences since the MainHUD touch control button is hidden to all non-touch devices.

Hides all touch control schemes if on a non-touch device.

## Summary

This PR introduces support for a new "tar index" mode in the EROFS snapshotter and differ

## Key Changes

- **docs/snapshotters/erofs.md**: Added documentation for the new tar index mode, including configuration and usage details.
- **internal/erofsutils/mount_linux.go**: 
  - Added `GenerateTarIndexAndAppendTar` to create a combined EROFS layer with a tar index and tar content.
  - Added `SupportGenerateFromTar` to detect mkfs.erofs tar mode support.
- **plugins/diff/erofs/differ_linux.go**: 
  - Refactored to support tar index mode via options.
  - Differentiated between standard and tar index conversion logic.
- **plugins/diff/erofs/plugin/plugin_linux.go**: 
  - Updated plugin config to support enabling tar index mode via TOML.
  - Checked for mkfs.erofs tar mode support during plugin initialization.

## Configuration
To enable tar index mode, set `enable_tar_index = true` in the differ plugin configuration.
